cognate: Two-verb merism 'eat and drink' with the same pair of PIE verbs: Ved. ad- + pā-/píba-, Gk ἔδ-/ἐσθί- + πίνω, Lat. edo + bibo, OCS jasti + piti. Ved. addhí and Gk ἔσθι (whence ἐσθίω) both continue the imperative *h₁éd-dʰi, and Ved. píba- = Lat. bibe/bibat (*pí-ph₃-e-).
drift_or_renewal: 'Drink' renewed in Germanic (Goth. etun jah drugkun) and, recalled, in Hittite (ed- + eku-). 'Eat' renewed by τρώγω in the Hippocratic 2.134 s12 instance (πινέτω ... τρωγέτω).
shared_syntax: Two coordinated or juxtaposed verbs, 'eat' then 'drink' or the reverse, as imperatives or jussives (addhí ... píba ca; ἐσθιέτω ... πινέτω; esse ... bibat; Od. ἐσθίετε ... πίνετε), with the food or drink as object (οἶνον πινέτω ~ bibat uinum).
context: In the slab both Greek and Latin are prescriptions for a sick person's diet: Hippocratic gynaecology and Cato's brassica cure (CatAgr 156.1 gives the tight coordinated pair ederis bibes que; 157.13 is conditional, esse ... bibat). The Vedic case is an invitation to a god to eat and drink an offering (RV 10.116.7: addhí ... píba). It matches the AVP 19.30.20 imperative pair addhi ... pibā, and Circe's invitation to her guests in Od. 10.460 (ἐσθίετε ... πίνετε). Caveat: 'eat and drink' is a near-universal merism, and both verbs are basic inherited vocabulary, so the match may come from lexical inheritance alone rather than from an inherited formula. The case rests on the cognate imperatives in congruent contexts of offering, hospitality and prescription. The Hittite ed-/eku- parallel and the addhí = ἔσθι equation come from memory, not from the corpora.

note: All 212 bundles read. Almost every bundle pairs a Hippocratic gynaecological recipe with a Cato De agri cultura recipe; the overlap is recipe vocabulary (wine, honey, give/drink, mix). One low-confidence claim: the 'eat and drink' merism. Rejected leads: melle dulcior ~ μέλιτος γλυκίων (no Greek comparative in the slab to anchor it); the night-and-day merism (generic); áditir mātā sá pitā sá putráḥ ~ Il. 6.429 (no congruent Greek passage in the slab).
